title: Synthetic-sorted token SLI telemetry and adaptive traffic-steering visualization
creator: Ravi Shah
description:
Goal: build a telemetry and dashboard surface that measures token-level latency SLIs in a way that isolates admission/ shed decisions, sequence-length bias, and regional variance using synthetic-sorted traffic. This ticket covers the instrumentation changes, ingestion schema, aggregation rules, alert bindings, and dashboard panels required to operate multi-region adaptive traffic steering and circuit break workflows.

Why: existing token SLIs are skewed by request size, KV-cache priming, and admission sampling. We need a reproducible synthetic harness that emits categorically sorted requests (by sequence length, model variant, route, and admission class) so SLO burn can be attributed to the right control plane — and so dashboards can visualize whether sheds are due to regional capacity, admission policy hysteresis, or model performance regressions.

High-level approach:
- Instrument runtime to emit per-request labels: region, shard_id, model_name, model_variant, route, tenant_id (hashed), sequence_length_bucket, admission_decision (admit|reject|early-exit), kv_cache_hit (true|false), response_tokens_count, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, latency_ms (end-to-end), per_token_latency_histogram (exposure buckets).
- Add two synthetic traffic generators in staging and canary: one that emits fixed-length sequences (short/medium/long) and one that emits realistic joint distribution from production traces trimmed for privacy. Both will annotate traffic with synthetic_tag for easy filtering.
- Telemetry pipeline: extend OTLP proto to include new fields; add mapping to our metrics backend (Datadog + Honeycomb event enrichment). Generate the following derived metrics: admit_token_count, shed_token_count, per_token_p50/p95/p99, token_latency_histogram_by_region, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_route, admission_reject_rate_by_model_variant.
- Aggregation rules: percentiles computed over admitted tokens only; histograms use fixed power-of-two buckets for per-token latency; synthetic-sorted SLI series computed as p95 across synthetic cohorts (length x variant x region).
- Dashboards: overview SLO burn, regional admission waterfall, admission decision-tree visualization, synthetic cohort SLI trend lines, model-variant comparison, top failing routes, and a drill-down panel for KV-cache priming impact.
- Alerts & runbook: define SLO burn alerts tied to synthetic cohort p95 and real traffic p99 (separate burn thresholds). Update the failover playbook to include when to trigger region-to-region traffic steering vs. graceful degradation.

Success criteria (short):
- Synthetic harness generating stable cohorts in staging and canary and visible in dashboards.
- New per-token metrics flowing to metrics backend for all admission decisions.
- Dashboards with baseline (last 14d) and canary overlays; SLO burn alerts firing in synthetic chaos tests.

Implementation risks / trade-offs:
- Increased cardinality: adding many new labels will raise metric storage costs. Mitigation: aggregate at ingest (drop tenant_id except hashed bucket) and materialize only cohorts we need.
- Latency of telemetry: histograms and high-cardinality labels increase ingest CPU; we will sample real traffic and run synthetic cohorts at controlled rates.
- Privacy: production traces used to seed synthetic generator must be scrubbed; use hashing and trimming.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype instrumentation in runtime branch (ENG-362711).
2) Wire OTLP mapping and test ingestion (ENG-362712).
3) Deploy synthetic harness to staging; run baseline collection for 7 days.
4) Create dashboard in internal Grafana / Datadog and validate queries.
5) Canary run with controlled failovers (region steal, blobbed gpu exhaustion) and tune alerts.

Metric names (proposal):
- redwood.tokens.admit.count
- redwood.tokens.shed.count
- redwood.tokens.per_token_latency.hist (buckets)
- redwood.tokens.p95_ms
- redwood.tokens.kv_cache_hit.rate
- redwood.admission.reject.rate

Notes: avoid adding tenant_id raw string to metrics; use tenant_hash_bucket label (0..127) for low-cardinality grouping.
